problem_statement:
After the apps change is applied, ostest_main.c includes <malloc.h> and the user_main test is expected to build and pass. With the kernel at the base commit, the build fails with:
ostest_main.c:113:40: error: ‘struct mallinfo’ has no member named ‘mxordblk’
The caller observes that the allocation statistics interface expected from the header included by the test is not usable with the kernel at the base commit. The required behavior is that the test compiles and user_main passes when using that interface, including the members the test accesses, and that the interface remains API-compatible with the expected system API.

superseded_statements.problem_statement: The test includes <malloc.h> to get the struct mallinfo type and the mallinfo() function. On the old kernel malloc.h does not exist (mallinfo/struct mallinfo are only in stdlib.h), so the test fails to compile; the required behavior is that struct mallinfo and mallinfo() are provided by malloc.h (included by kmalloc.h) so the test compiles and runs.
check_issues: `problem_statement` gives the fix away: "On the old kernel malloc.h does not exist (mallinfo/struct mallinfo are only in stdlib.h)"; "the required behavior is that struct mallinfo and mallinfo() are provided by malloc.h (included by kmalloc.h)". Describe only the observable symptom, its trigger and the required behavior, not what the code checks or must do internally
